This is the brief instruction I give to you: ‘Abandon desire for the impermanent. “But, venerable sir, how does one know, how does one see, so that in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no desire, no lust, no affection, no thirst, no passion, no fever, no craving? “Ānanda, when one sees as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is suffering,’ then in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no desire, no lust, no affection, no thirst, no passion, no fever, no craving. When one sees as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is the origin of suffering’... ‘This is the cessation of suffering’... ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering,’ then in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no desire, no lust, no affection, no thirst, no passion, no fever, no craving. “Venerable sir, how does one know, how does one see, so that in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit? “Ānanda, when one sees as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘All phenomena are non-self,’ then in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no I-making, mine-making, and the underlying tendency to conceit. “Venerable sir, how does one know, how does one see, so that in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no agitation and distress about what is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, reached, sought after, and examined by the mind? “Ānanda, when one sees as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘All phenomena are empty,’ then in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no agitation and distress about what is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, reached, sought after, and examined by the mind. “Venerable sir, how does one know, how does one see, so that in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no more conceiving? “Ānanda, when one sees as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘All phenomena are not to be clung to,’ then in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no more clinging. “Venerable sir, how does one know, how does one see, so that in regard to this body with its consciousness and all external phenomena, there is no more obsession?
